text: Lesson 22 named four real findings on Meridian Trust Bank's instance. This lesson designs the actual fix for each one — a redesigned role hierarchy, a real corrected ACL script, and a planned migration to the bank's existing single sign-on standard. This is remediation, not a second audit.

Finding one's fix: a new base role, meridian_itil_base, holds baseline access. Meridian_incident_approver and meridian_itil_l3 extend it through contains_roles instead of duplicating its grants from scratch. The three old near-duplicate roles are deactivated, not deleted, preserving their sys_audit history, and every affected user now holds exactly one role whose name says what it grants.

Finding two's fix brings annual_income up to the same pattern ssn already used, then goes further: the scripted ACL checks whether the viewer holds a senior override role, or holds the standard role and is actually assigned to that customer's underwriting case. A standard underwriter can no longer browse every customer's income data — only the cases genuinely assigned to them. The field's Audit flag is enabled at the same time, closing finding four for this field specifically.

Finding three's fix is a planned cutover, not a flag flipped in production. Exchange SAML metadata with the bank's existing Okta tenant in sub-production first, mapping assertions to existing accounts by email. Multi-factor authentication comes from Okta's existing mandatory policy automatically — no separate configuration inside ServiceNow at all. Exactly one local break-glass admin account stays active, tightly monitored, for an SSO outage only.

The migration sets one cutover date and disables local authentication for every other account that same day — no months-long state where both paths stay open, which is where real migrations stall. Role sprawl replaced by a legible hierarchy, a weak ACL replaced by a relationship-aware script with auditing enabled, and a dated plan to finally enforce the bank's own SSO standard.

Three findings redesigned with real role records, real ACL code, and a real migration plan. Lesson 24 closes the capstone with a full security review checklist covering every chapter of this course, and looks ahead to how these fixes get promoted safely across environments in the next course.
